subject: Rack-level networking, SSD local PV and cross-rack failover — preflight questions
messages:
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@northbridge.com>
To: logan_wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: NorthBridge SRE Team <sre@northbridge.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial rack / storage questions for Redwood Private deployment

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking this on. Were starting hardware prep for the Redwood Private deployment and have a few rack-level questions before we finalize procurement:

- Our goal: 3 racks in a single DC (A/B/C) with cross-rack service availability. We need guidance on recommended control-plane topology (dedicated control nodes per rack vs single rack + standby).
- Networking: Do you require jumbo frames (MTU 9000) across ToR switches? We have some Brocade switches currently that default to 1500.
- Storage: Were evaluating two options: leverage existing SAN for persistent volumes (FibreChannel) OR add NVMe SSDs to compute nodes for local PVs (fast KV cache + ephemeral). Thoughts on lifecycle and rebuild times?
- Encryption & compliance: Procurement will enforce AES-256 at rest for all customer data. How does that affect our CSI choices and backup/snapshot tooling?
- Acceptable node specs: minimum disk/IO targets for inference workloads (llm K/V cache and model shards).

I attached a rough topology diagram (topology-drawing-v1.pdf). Can you point us to the acceptance criteria we should include in the purchase order and any preflight tests your team runs?

Appreciate an initial checklist — were aiming to sign PO in two weeks.

Best,
Carlos Vega
Head of Infrastructure, NorthBridge Logistics

Attachments: topology-drawing-v1.pdf
From: logan_wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial rack / storage questions for Redwood Private deployment

Carlos — thanks for the diagram, this is exactly the right time to align before procurement. High-level checklist and recommendations below; Ill follow up with a short preflight runbook and a scheduling link for on-site validation.

Short answers up front:
- Control plane: we prefer a 3-control-node quorum spread across racks A/B/C with anti-affinity scheduling (one control in each rack). This avoids single-rack control-plane failure and keeps etcd healthy during rack maintenance.
- MTU: jumbo frames (9216) improve throughput for large model shards and RDMA/ROCE flows but only if every hop supports it. If your Brocades are stuck at 1500, we recommend leaving MTU 1500 and sizing for higher throughput or using link aggregation.
- Storage approach: hybrid is optimal. Use local NVMe on worker nodes for hot KV caches (small, high-iops PVs provisioned via local-volume CSI or rook-block for replication). Use a replicated distributed backend (Rook/Ceph or enterprise SAN with a CSI driver) for durable model artifacts and long-term persistence.
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest is compatible with both SAN and Ceph; if you use SAN ensure the CSI driver supports in-cloud keywrap or point to your HSM/KMS. For local NVMe, consider dm-crypt + LUKS on the host or an in-node encryption layer; well document keys/rotation expectations.
- Node sizing: for inference nodes (model shard + cache) we recommend:
  - CPU: 24 vCPU equivalent
  - Memory: 256-512GB depending on model size
  - Local NVMe: at least 2TB NVMe per node for caching tier with endurance class rated for write amplification (enterprise SSDs)
  - Network: 25Gbps min, 100Gbps preferred for cross-rack model transfer windows

Acceptance criteria (PO items to include):
- Control plane: 3 nodes live in separate racks, validated quorum failover (etcd survives a full rack outage)
- PV latency: <5ms read latency for hot-local SSD PVs under baseline load (well provide a perf tool)
- PV binding and mount success rate: >99% for preflight runs across 50 test PVs
- Snapshot/restore: successful encrypted snapshots and restores in target environment
- Network: validated path MTU or documented fallback and link aggregation configured on ToR

Im attaching our ops checklist (redwood-onprem-ops-checklist-v1.pdf) and will add a storage micro-benchmark we run during validation. Quick ask: can you confirm whether Rack B SAN will remain, or if you can commit to adding NVMe in at least two racks? If SAN remains, well include SAN-integration steps.

Next step: I can run a 60-minute validation call + test window next Tuesday. If you prefer, Marissa can outline the security/compliance requirements in more detail.

—Logan
VP, Field Deployments
Redwood Inference

2) What do you recommend for cross-rack replication for NVMe-local PVs? Can we run local-volume CSI + periodic replication to SAN/ceph, or should we rely on application-level replication?

Subject: Re: Initial rack / storage questions for Redwood Private deployment

Team — a few implementation notes from security and operations that should shape the design: 

1) Mixed backends in one cluster: supported but needs policy.
- Kubernetes supports multiple StorageClasses. We recommend explicit StorageClass naming (eg: sc-nvme-hot, sc-san-durable, sc-ceph-repl). Add PodStorageConstraints in our Helm charts so pods express topologyAffinity and tolerations for the right storage.
- Operator guardrails: set reclaimPolicy=Retain for critical model artifacts until backups verified.

2) Replication approach for local NVMe: application-level replication for model shards is safest (Redwood runtime already supports model shard redundancy). For KV cache, use local-volume CSI + async replication to Ceph/SAN snapshots for cold data fallback. We favor Rook-Ceph (if allowed) because it provides CRUSH-based replication across racks and integrates with KMS for encryption.

3) SAN integration: If you must keep FibreChannel SAN, we recommend the vendor CSI driver + a dedicated storage node pool (storage-nodes) that expose persistent volumes via the CSI. Avoid using hostPath for production.

4) Kube and node tuning (quick checklist):
- kubelet eviction thresholds: set imagefs.available<10% and nodefs.available<8% with eviction grace periods for model artifacts
- pod anti-affinity for shard placement: preferSpread rule by topology.kubernetes.io/zone mapped to rack label
- pv-provisioner performance limits: increase volumeAttachLimit for nodes with many local volumes
- filesystem: XFS for Ceph/Rook; ext4 OK for LUKS encrypted NVMe (add fstrim cron).

5) Security: integrate your HSM with our keywrap flow. For local NVMe encryption we recommend using LUKS2 with a KMS-backed key that Redwood can rotate via a documented API call.

6) Failover validation: include an acceptance test where Rack B is powered off and we validate model inference continuity with degraded throughput but no data loss. That test should be in the PO.

Ive opened JIRA-NB-4123 to track the SAN CSI driver integration and added a task for a small Rook PoC if you can provide two nodes with NVMe in at least two racks.

If everyone is aligned Ill schedule the validation window and share preflight scripts.

—Marissa
Director, Field Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks all for the quick responses — summary and next steps below.

Summary decisions:
- Control plane: 3-node control spread across racks A/B/C (etcd quorum)
- Networking: Keep MTU 1500 for now; configure LACP on compute links and document jumbo-frame upgrade path for later
- Storage: Hybrid approach (local NVMe for hot cache, SAN or Rook/Ceph for durable volumes). Willow (storage team) will provision a storage-node pool mapped to FibreChannel CSI for Rack B.
- Encryption: NorthBridge HSM to be integrated for keywrap; for local NVMe we will use LUKS2 with keys stored in the HSM/KMS and rotation handled by Redwood ops API.
- Tests required in PO: etcd quorum failover, PV perf (baseline), encrypted snapshot/restore, and Rack B power-off failover test.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- NorthBridge: confirm whether NVMe can be added to two racks by 2026-08-06 (Carlos)
- Redwood (Marissa): create preflight test plan + scripts and share by 2026-07-27 (JIRA-NB-4123)
- Redwood (Logan): schedule 60-min validation window week of 2026-08-09 and provide perf benchmarks to include in PO
- NorthBridge: provide SAN CSI driver details and credentials for test environment (sre@northbridge.com)

Attachments I referenced here: topology-drawing-v1.pdf, redwood-onprem-ops-checklist-v1.pdf, storage-test-results.csv. Drive folder with full design: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cDesignDoc

If that matches your expectations, reply with "ACK" and well lock dates. If not, call me and well walk the open items.
